identificationModule.briefTitle: Cryoablation Versus Lumpectomy in Early-Stage Breast Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: Cryoablation as Alternative for Lumpectomy in Early-Stage Breast Cancer: The CRYSTAL Trial

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The goal of this randomised controlled trial is to compare ipsilateral breast cancer recurrence rates in patients with early-stage breast cancer between patients treated with breast conserving surgery and patient treated with percutaneous cryo-ablation.

designInfo.interventionModelDescription: This is a multicenter randomized phase III non-inferiority trial with two arms: percutaneous cryoablation and breastconserving surgery. The randomization ratio is 1:1, stratified by center, tumor size (\< / \> 1 cm) and Bloom Richardson grade. All eligible patients will consecutively be included and randomized. Crossover is only possible for patients allocated to the cryoablation arm.

primaryOutcomes.description: Proportion of ipsilateral breast cancer recurrences (IBTR) after 5 years in both study arms.

secondaryOutcomes.description: The proportion of complications within 30 days (percentage Clavien-Dindo classification).
Regional breast cancer recurrences, defined as clinically, radiologically, and/or histologically confirmed recurrence in regional lymph nodes.

Disease free survival (DFS) is defined as the time from date of intervention to the first occurrence of recurrent disease of the same histological characteristics as the primary tumor and in the same quadrant as the primary tumor
Overall survival (OS) is defined as the time from breast cancer diagnosis to death from any cause.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: through study completion, an average of 15 years

secondaryOutcomes.description: o assess cosmetic outcomes following treatment with cryoablation or lumpectomy using the BCTOS-13 and BREAST-Q questionnaires at specified follow-up visits, and objective assessment using BCCT.core software. Higher scores indicate better cosmetic outcomes.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: at baseline, 6 months and 1 year after the intervention

secondaryOutcomes.description: Hospital-related costs, including expenses made due to additional findings on inclusion MRI
To assess out-of-hospital medical and non-medical costs and productivity losses using the iMTA Medical Consumption Questionnaire (iMCQ) and iMTA Productivity Cost Questionnaire (iPCQ) questionnaires.
To assess general health-related quality of life using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire, with higher scores indicating better health status
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At baseline, 6 months after the intervention, 1 and 5 years after the intervention

secondaryOutcomes.description: To assess cancer-specific quality of life using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and EORTC QLQ-BR23 questionnaires. Higher scores indicate better functioning or greater symptom burden depending on the subscale.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At baseline, 6 months after the intervention, 1 and 5 years after the intervention

secondaryOutcomes.description: The negative predictive-, and diagnostic value of MRI for incomplete ablation

secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: For the duration of the study, most likely within 2 weeks after the intervention

secondaryOutcomes.description: The proportion of acute and long-term breast irradiation toxicity (radiation dermatitis, superficial or deep connective tissue fibrosis, chest wall pain, localized edema) using common toxicity criteria (CTCAE v5.0) and cosmetic questionnaires
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At baseline, prior to radiation, 1 year and 5 years after the intervention

secondaryOutcomes.description: To estimate the incremental cost-utility ratio (ICUR). Higher ICUR values indicate higher costs per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained.

otherOutcomes.description: To explore patient- or tumor-related factors that may influence complete ablation or surgical outcomes, including breast density and other relevant parameters.
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: until the end of the study, which is an average of 5 years

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Women
2. Age \> 60 years
3. Postmenopausal (no menstrual period for at least 12 months or in case of an intra-uterine device (IUD) hormone levels that indicate the menopause: follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) \> 20 IE/l and estradiol \< 100 pmol/l)
4. Histopathological confirmed primary invasive ER+/HER2- type breast cancer
5. Bloom Richardson grade 1 or 2 (low or intermediate malignancy grade)
6. Unilateral and unifocal breast cancer
7. A clinical T1N0M0 tumor (≤ 2cm and N0 on US and/or MRI), without distant metastases. The largest diameter measured will be used to determine eligibility.
8. Tumor should be visible and well delineated (all borders of the tumor should be visible) on ultrasound at diagnosis and during the procedure.
9. Sufficient knowledge of the Dutch language to complete the questionnaires
10. To be able to give written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

1. History of invasive breast cancer
2. Breast augmentation
3. BRCA-1 or 2 gene mutation carrier
4. Lobular carcinoma
5. Triple negative breast cancer
6. Multifocality
7. HER2-neu overexpressing tumors
8. Lymph vascular invasion (LVI) on core needle biopsy or histopathological confirmed after lumpectomy
9. Indication for neoadjuvant systemic therapy
10. Intraductal component \> 25% of the diameter of the invasive tumor on MRI, complete area of the primary tumor should not exceed 2cm.
11. Allergic to local anesthetics
12. Electrical devices and/or implants that are not compatible with MRI
13. Current severe breast infection
14. Uncorrectable coagulopathy
15. Hemodynamic instability
16. Respiratory instability
17. Refraining from adjuvant radiotherapy
18. Indication for oncoplastic surgery (surgical volume replacement techniques e.g. LICAP)
